extracted.intended_audience: college/university instructors and course designers using or evaluating peer-assessment tools (especially Kritik users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for implementing calibrated peer review within an online peer-assessment workflow so student graders are calibrated to instructor standards and their grading influence is weighted accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear grading standards defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective automated grading software must have clear grading standards defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that clear grading standards are a prerequisite for automated grading to work well, particularly for short answer or written assignments where instructors need to define what constitutes acceptable performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified solutions stated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating specified solutions (model answers or exemplars) is listed alongside grading standards as necessary for automated grading accuracy; these serve as the instructor's benchmark during calibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The product claim is that automated grading must produce accurate results; calibration is presented as a mechanism to improve accuracy and reduce biased/inaccurate grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric-based assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Students anonymously evaluate their peer's submissions through rubric-based assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rubric-based assessments as the core instrument for peer grading; anonymity is highlighted (students grade anonymously), and rubrics provide the criteria students use both in regular peer grading and in calibration exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration exemplars: professor selects three creations
rubrics_metrics.description: A professor will select, review and evaluate three creations of a previously finalized Kritik activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration requires the instructor to choose exemplar submissions (three) from the activity and grade them as the gold-standard against which student graders will be compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student calibration task: evaluate same exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will then evaluate the same three creations and have their evaluations provided for those same creations compared with the evaluations provided by the professor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students perform the same rubric-based assessment on the instructor-chosen exemplars so the system can measure how closely each student's grading aligns with the professor's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration scoring: closeness to professor increases grading score
rubrics_metrics.description: Students who have marked in line with how the professor did will get a higher grading score for the calibration activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform compares student and professor evaluations; students whose marks closely match the instructor receive higher calibration scores, demonstrating stronger grader reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for poor or low-effort graders
rubrics_metrics.description: Students who marked poorly or with little effort will be penalized with a lower grading score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor alignment or low-effort grading reduces a student's calibration score, which decreases their subsequent grading influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted peer influence based on calibration score
rubrics_metrics.description: Students who ranked grading points from the calibration activity will have a higher weight as they evaluate their peer submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration scores are used as weights when aggregating peer evaluations: graders who calibrated well have more influence on final grades of peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation score as weighted average
rubrics_metrics.description: The creation score is an overall weighted average of the evaluations that a student received on their submission. In this case, the weight is the peer evaluators grading score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final submission scores are computed by weighting each peer evaluator's assessment by that evaluator's calibration-derived grading score; this ties evaluator reliability directly into student outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended calibration frequency (1–2 times per term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administering a calibration activity 1-2 times over the whole term is more than enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page recommends running calibration only a small number of times (once or twice) across a term to establish grader reliability without overburdening students or instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended assignment volume to improve evaluation scores
rubrics_metrics.description: With at least 6-7 Kritik activities by the end of the term, you can expect to see an exponential increase in the student's Evaluation score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using multiple peer-assessment activities across the term (6–7 or more) is recommended to allow students to practice grading and to see improvements in their calibration/evaluation scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify strong peer evaluators to support grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Students who grade closely to you indicate how well they are absorbing the context of the assignment requirements and rubric criteria. You can count on these students alike to the TA's to provide effective assessments and feedback that will further support their peers in the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use calibration to surface reliable student graders who can be relied upon for higher-quality peer feedback or to serve TA-like roles; this is both a quality-control and pedagogical benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gamification to motivate grader improvement ('Grade Power')
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Grade Power' gamification system allows students to keep track of their improvement throughout the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting calibration progress and grading scores as gamified metrics motivates students to improve their grading accuracy and engagement with rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome: improved grading accuracy and less grade inflation
rubrics_metrics.description: You are guaranteed less inflated grades through calibrated peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration is promoted as reducing grade inflation and increasing precision of peer-assigned grades versus uncalibrated peer assessment.
